description: variant-fixed's layout and copybook over a file whose second record carries an entry no arm covers: a kind byte M, where the arms select on D and on F. The read stops there, so the answer is the first record and a failure, and the record the failure is in contributes nothing -- a record read as far as its second entry is not a record. What the entry is about is that the refusal happens at all: there is no default arm, a producer cannot write one, and a consumer that fell through to the last arm would read seven bytes of an address it has no description of as a state and a ZIP. The record it is in is one the layout does describe -- its type byte is A and the transition matched it -- so this is the second of the two failures docs/ir/SPEC.md requires a consumer to tell apart, and an adopter sent to the first for it spends the day on a record type they already have. The diagnostic's words are the generator's own and are not compared; what is compared is that reading failed, and that it failed after the record listed.
source: docs/ir/SPEC.md, "A predicate on an arm reads one occurrence" -- "Where no arm matches, a consumer MUST report it, and MUST NOT fall through to the last arm or leave the occurrence's items unset" -- with "A variant is chosen once per occurrence" and "When two match, and when none does"; docs/layout/SPEC.md, "A discriminator for a redefine inside a table"; docs/conformance/SPEC.md, "A file the reader refused"; its layout and copybook are variant-fixed's.
